Shoals Marine Lab

Shoals Marine Laboratory is a seasonal field station on Appledore Island, the largest of the Isles of Shoals, a cluster of rocky islands about six miles off the coast of Maine and New Hampshire. It is run jointly by Cornell University and the University of New Hampshire.

This poster gathers life from the island’s intertidal zone, the stretch of rocky shore that floods and drains with every tide.

Visit the Shoals Marine Lab website

Marshall Mumford

Marshall is a self-taught photographer from Delaware. He took Marine Mammal Biology at Shoals in 2024, then returned as a SURG in 2025. In 2026, he was a TA for six courses, during which he photographed all the creatures above, sourced by Kate Lockridge and instructors and students of various courses throughout the summer from the intertidal region around Appledore Island.

See more of his work at mrm.photography

The Intertidal

The intertidal is the strip of shore between the highest and lowest tides. Twice a day the sea covers it, and twice a day it drains away, leaving its residents exposed to sun, wind, rain and air.

Life here has to survive both worlds. Barnacles and periwinkles seal themselves shut to keep from drying out, rockweeds float up toward the light when the water returns, and crabs, fish and sea stars shelter in tide pools and under seaweed until the tide comes back. Each creature settles at the height on the shore it can best tolerate, which is why the rocks show bands of different life from top to bottom.

On the rocky shores of Appledore Island, this narrow zone holds a remarkable variety of animals and seaweeds, from tiny springtails and skeleton shrimp to lobsters and kelp.
